question.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}=4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,-8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨0,-4,0⟩\times ⟨-4,0,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & \,\,-4 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-16\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =16\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}=\frac{{4}^{3}}{\,16\,}=4.\end{aligned}
$$
